assistantMessageEvent.content:
I'm spotting several bugs: commits happening even when the flight is stale and deleting newer entries from pending, rejections never clearing the pending cache so failures get stuck forever, and needing to verify the invalidation logic only clears entries that are still current rather than ones that may have been superseded.

With a generation token approach, detached flights can't corrupt state even if invalidate or set runs mid-flight — overwriting a set value with a stale commit is prevented. I'm also checking the ttlMs=0 edge case where values expire immediately, confirming get and size correctly discard them, and verifying that an active flight and an expired value can't coexist under the token scheme since flights only run when no value exists.

Rejections are shared correctly across all waiters on the same flight, and a detached flight's rejection shouldn't incorrectly invalidate a newer flight's state — that all checks out with per-flight identity.

For cleanup, I can use the promise itself as the flight's token stored in the pending map, since it's assigned before any `.then` callbacks fire asynchronously, so identity checks remain safe. On successful resolution the flight commits its value only if it's still the current pending entry for that key, and on rejection it just clears itself from pending without disturbing anything newer — a manual `set()` or `clear()` naturally short-circuits this since the flight will no longer match what's stored.

One more edge case: if `load` recursively calls `get` on its own key while still in flight, the pending map already holds the promise, so it should just return that same in-flight promise rather than starting a new one.

I'm also checking a few boundary conditions: expired values get silently dropped during reads without touching any pending flight, `now()` is side-effect free so call count doesn't matter, and a flight can only exist while there's no live value since `set` always detaches it first. For TTL validation, `Number.isFinite` correctly rejects strings and NaN without coercion, and `-0` passes the "not negative" check harmlessly.

Other cases line up too: missing or null options just throw via destructuring, sync invalidate/set calls happening inside a load's microtask correctly bypass the eventual commit, and loads touching other keys stay independent. I'm now ready to patch flight.js and then write a quick verification script covering the set-during-load scenario.

Found the root cause in `src/flight.js`: the `.then` always commits/deletes regardless of whether `invalidate`/`set`/`clear` already detached the flight, causing stale writes, TTL resets, and broken dedup—plus rejected flights never get removed from `pending`, blocking retries. Fix: only let the current flight (verified by promise identity) commit or remove itself, on both success and rejection.

content.thinking:
I'm spotting several bugs: commits happening even when the flight is stale and deleting newer entries from pending, rejections never clearing the pending cache so failures get stuck forever, and needing to verify the invalidation logic only clears entries that are still current rather than ones that may have been superseded.

With a generation token approach, detached flights can't corrupt state even if invalidate or set runs mid-flight — overwriting a set value with a stale commit is prevented. I'm also checking the ttlMs=0 edge case where values expire immediately, confirming get and size correctly discard them, and verifying that an active flight and an expired value can't coexist under the token scheme since flights only run when no value exists.

Rejections are shared correctly across all waiters on the same flight, and a detached flight's rejection shouldn't incorrectly invalidate a newer flight's state — that all checks out with per-flight identity.

For cleanup, I can use the promise itself as the flight's token stored in the pending map, since it's assigned before any `.then` callbacks fire asynchronously, so identity checks remain safe. On successful resolution the flight commits its value only if it's still the current pending entry for that key, and on rejection it just clears itself from pending without disturbing anything newer — a manual `set()` or `clear()` naturally short-circuits this since the flight will no longer match what's stored.

One more edge case: if `load` recursively calls `get` on its own key while still in flight, the pending map already holds the promise, so it should just return that same in-flight promise rather than starting a new one.

I'm also checking a few boundary conditions: expired values get silently dropped during reads without touching any pending flight, `now()` is side-effect free so call count doesn't matter, and a flight can only exist while there's no live value since `set` always detaches it first. For TTL validation, `Number.isFinite` correctly rejects strings and NaN without coercion, and `-0` passes the "not negative" check harmlessly.

Other cases line up too: missing or null options just throw via destructuring, sync invalidate/set calls happening inside a load's microtask correctly bypass the eventual commit, and loads touching other keys stay independent. I'm now ready to patch flight.js and then write a quick verification script covering the set-during-load scenario.

Found the root cause in `src/flight.js`: the `.then` always commits/deletes regardless of whether `invalidate`/`set`/`clear` already detached the flight, causing stale writes, TTL resets, and broken dedup—plus rejected flights never get removed from `pending`, blocking retries. Fix: only let the current flight (verified by promise identity) commit or remove itself, on both success and rejection.

Since callbacks run asynchronously, the promise binding gets initialized fine. I'll write a quick throwaway script to check the contract paths, placing it in the current directory rather than test/, then delete it once I'm done.
